_strings.@@67219f8f41c0: Treaty conformity — MA conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from MA income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the MA return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Net result: treaty-exempt income is NOT re-taxed by MA, so conforms = true — but the mechanism is an EXPLICIT DEDUCTION, not passive federal-AGI conformity. Important nuance: MA's Form 1 does NOT start from federal AGI. It builds Massachusetts gross income from its own categories. Line 3 (Wages) is taken from W-2 state wages (Box 16), and Massachusetts gross income can include items not subject to U.S. income tax. So treaty-exempt income that an employer reports in state wages would otherwise land in MA income. MA neutralizes this with the dedicated Schedule Y, Line 4 deduction: 'Amounts Excludible Under MGL Ch 41, § 111F or U.S. Tax Treaty Included in Form 1, Line 3' — the 2024 Form 1 instructions repeat the 2023 rule: a taxpayer with income exempt under a United States tax treaty enters the excludible amount that was included in Form 1, line 3 on Schedule Y line 4 and fills in the treaty oval. Because Schedule Y reduces income, the treaty-exempt amount is deducted back out and is not taxed. PRACTICAL NOTE: unlike a pure federal-AGI conformity state where treaty income flows out automatically, in MA the taxpayer must affirmatively claim the Schedule Y, Line 4 deduction (and fill the treaty oval) — if treaty wages appear in W-2 Box 16/Form 1 line 3 and the deduction is not claimed, the income would be taxed. Source: 2024 Form 1 Instructions, Schedule Y Line 4 (income exempt under a U.S. tax treaty) and Line 3 (Wages, Salaries, Tips).
_strings.@@6d13cf5df3c9: Child and Family Tax Credit — Resident (or part-year resident for the period of residency) maintaining a household that includes a qualifying individual: a dependent under age 13, a dependent age 65 or older or disabled, or a dependent or spouse physically or mentally incapable of self-care who principally lives with the taxpayer. NEW for 2024 (TIR 24-13): a noncustodial parent may claim the credit for a child dependent age 13 or older who is physically or mentally incapable of caring for himself or herself. Cannot be claimed by a full-year nonresident.

state_tax.work_common_tail: 0. Tax line: Form 1 line 22: 'TAX ON 5.0% INCOME (from tax table). If line 21 is more than $24,000, multiply by .05' (line 21 = TOTAL TAXABLE 5.0% INCOME = line 19 income after exemptions + line 20 Schedule B interest and dividend income). Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): age_65 ($700 — Form 1 line 2c: $700 per age-65-or-over-before-2025 box (You/Spouse) — the visible face prints '× $ 700 = 2c'; its text layer reads '$1,700' because a separate '1,' text object is invisible, which an earlier extraction copied (corrected 2026-10-02 from a render of the blank). NOT applied by calc.state_tax — subtract it from the supplied base or compute line 2c on the form.); blind ($2,200 — Form 1 line 2d: $2,200 per blindness box (You/Spouse). NOT applied by calc.state_tax — subtract it from the supplied base or compute line 2d on the form.) This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Figures unchanged from 2023 (both passes re-verified for 2024): the 5.0% rate, the line 2a-2d exemption amounts, and the $24,000 tax-table cutoff are identical; the 4% surtax threshold INDEXED UP to $1,053,750 (2023: $1,000,000), and the former line 5 up-to-$100/$200 Massachusetts bank interest exemption is REPEALED for 2024 (line 5 is now plain 'Massachusetts bank interest'). Base guidance: supply 2024 Form 1 line 17 ('5.0% INCOME AFTER DEDUCTIONS' = line 10 TOTAL 5.0% INCOME minus line 16 total deductions) PLUS line 20 (interest and dividend income from Schedule B, line 38) — i.e., the Part B 5.0% taxable income BEFORE the line 18 exemptions. The op subtracts the line 2a personal exemption (shipped per filing status in standard_deduction) and $1,000 per dependent (line 2b), reproducing lines 18-21, then multiplies by 5% (line 22). Filers with line 2c-2f exemptions (age 65+ $700 each, blindness $2,200 each, medical/dental from U.S. Schedule A line 4, adoption) must subtract those amounts from the supplied base themselves. Modeling decision — standard_deduction carries the Form 1 line 2a PERSONAL EXEMPTION: Massachusetts has NO standard deduction; line 2a is a fixed per-filing-status base reduction ($4,400 single or married filing separately, $6,800 head of household, $8,800 married filing jointly) and ships in the per-status standard_deduction slot because the per-person 'personal' exemption key cannot represent the $6,800 head-of-household amount. Pass exemptions_count=0 — the taxpayer/spouse exemption is already inside the per-status amount. CRITICAL — 4% surtax NOT modeled: 'Starting with tax year 2023, personal income taxpayers must pay an additional 4% (4% surtax) on taxable income over $1,000,000, increased annually for inflation (surtax threshold). For the 2024 tax year, the threshold is $1,053,750' (2024 Form 1 instructions; TIR 23-12 and the 4% Surtax FAQs). The surtax is computed on Schedule 4% Surtax and entered on Form 1 line 28b, and it applies to the SUM of all classes of taxable income (the 5.0% Part B income modeled here PLUS Schedule B 8.5%/12% income PLUS Schedule D long-term capital gains) over $1,053,750. It is NOT a marginal bracket of the 5.0% schedule — encoding it as one would misstate Massachusetts' class-separated system. If total taxable income across all classes exceeds $1,053,750, complete Schedule 4% Surtax on the form. Class separation (PA-like): Massachusetts taxes income classes separately, and this op computes ONLY the Form 1 line 22 tax on 5.0% income. Not modeled: Schedule B 8.5% income (line 23a x .085 — short-term capital gains and certain other gains), 12% income (line 23b x .12 — collectibles, subject to a 50% deduction), and Schedule D long-term capital gain tax (line 24). Never merge those classes into the supplied base. Tax-table mandate: 'If line 21 is less than $24,000, find the proper tax by using the tax tables found in the back of this booklet. If line 21 is greater than $24,000 multiply by 0.05' (Line 22 instructions, unchanged for 2024). Below $24,000 the filed form uses the booklet table, which can differ from exact multiplication by a small amount within a table band; the fetched instructions capture did not include the table pages, so the band structure was not re-verified this session. Optional 5.85% rate (NOT modeled): Form 1 line 22 carries an oval to voluntarily pay tax at 5.85% on income otherwise taxed at 5.0%; the election does not apply to 8.5%/12% items. Excess exemptions: if line 18 exemptions exceed line 17, the form sets line 19 to 0 and the excess may be applied against interest and dividend income and 8.5%/12% income (Schedule B line 36 via the instructions worksheet), then against long-term capital gains (Schedule D line 20). Because this op subtracts the exemptions from the combined line 17 + line 20 base, the offset against Part B interest/dividends is reproduced automatically; the offset against the 8.5%/12% and long-term-gain classes is NOT modeled. No Tax Status / Limited Income Credit (Form 1 lines 27-29, NOT modeled): Massachusetts AGI of $8,000 or less (single), $14,400 or less plus $1,000 per dependent (head of household), or $16,400 or less plus $1,000 per dependent (married filing jointly) qualifies for No Tax Status — line 28 tax becomes 0 (married filing separately never qualifies). Limited Income Credit ranges: up to $14,000 single; $14,400-$25,200 plus $1,750 per dependent HoH; $16,400-$28,700 plus $1,750 per dependent MFJ. Check the Massachusetts AGI worksheet before relying on the computed tax. Massachusetts gross income is built from MA's OWN categories, not federal AGI: Form 1 line 3 wages come from W-2 state wages (Box 16); income exempt under a U.S. tax treaty that landed in line 3 must be deducted on Schedule Y line 4 (fill the treaty oval). The header boxes a/b (federal total income / federal AGI) are informational only.
